desc:
Chatbot reports on top and unanswered questions show what customers really ask and where your assistant falls short. Ecom Swift LLC reads a period of real chats, groups them by topic and applies a first round of improvements.

## What is a chatbot conversation report?

A chatbot conversation report is a structured summary of what customers asked, how the assistant answered and where it failed. It groups hundreds of chats into topics, lists the most frequent questions, flags the ones left unanswered and counts how often chats were passed to staff.

A launched chatbot is not finished. Real visitors use words you did not expect, ask about things nobody planned for and sometimes get wrong answers that nobody notices. The chat log holds all of this, but nobody has time to read thousands of lines.

## Why reading real chats is the fastest way to improve

Guessing what customers want is slow and often wrong. The conversations show it directly. A question that appears fifty times deserves a clear, prominent answer. A question the bot misses again and again points to a gap in your content. A handoff reason that repeats may reveal a product, policy or page that confuses people.

These findings often go beyond the chatbot. If visitors keep asking about shipping costs, your product pages may not show them clearly. If they keep asking how to cancel, the process may be hidden. The report becomes a list of fixes for the whole business, not only the bot.

## How improvements change results

Each missing answer you add removes a failure point. The next visitor with that question gets help instead of a dead end, and your team receives one less repeat message. Corrections to wrong answers matter even more, because a confident error costs trust and sometimes money.

Improvement works best in small, targeted rounds. Fixing the biggest gaps first gives the most benefit for the least effort. The tracking sheet we provide with larger packages lets you repeat the process each month without starting from scratch.

## What a useful chatbot report includes

- The most common questions, ranked by how often they appear.
- Questions the assistant answered well, so you know what to protect.
- Questions it missed or answered wrongly.
- Reasons chats were passed to a person.
- Topics grouped in plain categories you can act on.
- Examples of real wording customers used.
- Suggested new answers, with drafts ready to add.
- Corrections for answers that were inaccurate or out of date.
- Content ideas for your website, based on repeated questions.
- A simple sheet you can update each month.

## What we do

We start by obtaining your chat history from the chatbot you already run, whether we built it or someone else did. We read the conversations, remove private details from anything we share and sort the questions into topics.

Then we compare what customers asked with what the assistant could do. The Basic package delivers a one-time report on top questions, unanswered ones and handoff reasons. The Standard package adds fixes for the biggest gaps: new answers, corrections and a before and after look at one topic. The Premium package covers a larger set of chats, adds content ideas for your site, supplies a monthly tracking sheet and includes a call to walk through the findings.

Ongoing monthly reviews are not part of these packages and are quoted separately if you want them. We also make no promise about customer satisfaction or sales, since those depend on many things beyond the bot.

## What to do, and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Share chats from a normal period, not only a quiet or busy week.
- Decide which topics matter most before the work starts.
- Act on website fixes the report suggests.
- Repeat the exercise regularly so improvements build up.
- Keep sensitive customer details out of any file you share.

**Avoid:**
- Judging the bot only by a handful of memorable chats.
- Adding answers without checking them against current policy.
- Ignoring topics that seem small but repeat often.
- Treating every unanswered question as equally important.
- Sharing logs that contain payment details.

## Who this service is for

This service suits a business whose chatbot has been live for a while and who suspects it is missing questions. It suits a manager who wants evidence to decide what to fix first. It also suits a team that inherited a chatbot built by someone else and needs to understand how it performs.

## What we need from you

An export or view of your chat history, and a note of anything that must stay private. You need an existing chatbot with real conversations in it. We ask for access to the chatbot as a team member or collaborator, so we can add answers if you choose a package that includes fixes. We never need your password.
